chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

One day, Dawud (peace be upon him) went out to recite the Psalms. Whenever he recited the Psalms, there would not remain a mountain, a stone, a bird, nor a beast except that it would respond to him. He kept walking until he reached a mountain, and upon that mountain was a cloistered prophet called Hizqil. When he heard the echo of the mountains and the voices of the beasts and the birds, he knew that it was Dawud (peace be upon him). So Dawud said: O Hizqil! Do you permit me to climb up to you? He said: No. So Dawud (peace be upon him) wept. Then Allah, exalted is His majesty, revealed to him: O Hizqil! Do not humiliate Dawud, and ask Me for well-being. So Hizqil stood, took the hand of Dawud, and raised him up to him. Then Dawud said: O Hizqil! Have you ever been tempted to sin? He said: No. He said: Have you ever felt conceit from your state of worshiping Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? He said: No. He said: Have you inclined toward the world and desired to take from its lusts and pleasures? He said: Yes indeed, perhaps it has occurred in my heart. He said: What do you do when that happens? He said: I enter this ravine and reflect upon what is in it. He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) entered that ravine, and there was an iron bed with a decomposed skull and withered bones upon it. And there was an iron tablet with writing upon it. Dawud (peace be upon him) read it and it said: I am Arwa Shalam. I ruled for a thousand years, I built a thousand cities, and I deflowered a thousand virgins. Yet in the end, dust became my bed, stones became my pillow, worms and snakes became my neighbours. So whoever sees me, let him not be deceived by the world.

key_terms.أروى شلم: Arwa Shalam — an ancient king whose epitaph serves as a lesson about worldly impermanence
key_terms.الزبور: The Psalms (Zabur) — the holy scripture revealed to Prophet Dawud
key_terms.الشعب: The ravine/cave — a place of contemplation and spiritual reflection
key_terms.العجب: Self-conceit/wonder — spiritual pride that can afflict even devout worshipers
key_terms.حزقيل: Hizqil (Ezekiel) — a prophet who lived as a hermit devoted to worship

ai.seo_question: What lesson about worldly attachment did Prophet Dawud learn from Hizqil and the inscription of Arwa Shalam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a powerful story of Prophet Dawud (David) who, while reciting the Psalms with all of creation responding to his voice, encountered Prophet Hizqil (Ezekiel) living as a hermit on a mountaintop. Initially refused entry, Dawud was admitted after divine intervention. Their conversation explores three spiritual tests: temptation to sin, spiritual conceit from worship, and worldly attachment. Hizqil admitted only to worldly temptation, which he combated by visiting a nearby cave containing the remains of a once-great king named Arwa Shalam. The king's iron epitaph declares he ruled for a thousand years, built a thousand cities, and had a thousand wives, yet ended with dust as his bed and worms as his neighbors. This narrative tradition teaches that even the greatest worldly power is ultimately reduced to nothing, serving as an antidote to worldly attachment.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to me from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

One day, Dawud (as) went to recite the Psalms. Whenever he would recite the Psalms, there would not remain a mountain, a stone, a bird, nor a creature except that it would repeat after him. So, he did not stop walking until he reached a mountain. Upon that mountain was a cloistered prophet called Hizqil. When he heard the sound of the mountains and the voices of the creatures and the birds, he knew that it was Dawud (as). So, Dawud said: O Hizqil! Do you permit me to climb up to you? He said: No. So, Dawud (as) wept. So, Allah revealed to him: "O Hizqil! Do not humiliate Dawud and ask Me for My forgiveness." So, Hizqil stood, took the hand of Dawud, and helped him up to him. So, Dawud said: O Hizqil! Have you ever been tempted to sin? He said: No. He said: Have you ever been alarmed by your state of worshiping Allah? He said: No. He said: Have you went into this world and wanted to take from its lustful and pleasurable things? He said: Of course -- perhaps it came to my heart. He said: What do you do when that happens? He said: I go to this cave and I contemplate over it. He said: So, Dawud (as) went to that cave and came across an iron bed with a decomposed skull and withering bones atop it. He came across an iron tablet with writing on it. Dawud (as) read it and it said: "I am Arwa Shalam. I ruled for one thousand years, I built one thousand cities, and I had sex with one thousand virgins. Yet, in the end, dust became my bed, rocks became my masters, and worms and snakes became my neighbours. To whoever sees me: do not be deceived by this world."
